reaction.episode: CORRECTION episode, data through Nov 27 and not stale: SPX -6.97% from its 120-day high, 3.93% below its 50-day and 0.77% below its 200-day; SMH -34.5% and NVDA -38.2% from their highs, both BELOW Zone 2; VIX 23.81 rolling over from a 28.29 five-day high; HY OAS 3.77, calm; mechanical capitulation tally 2 of 4.
reaction.invalidation: SMH or NVDA reclaiming Zone 2 on a close with the tally at 3 of 4 or better and SPX reclaiming its 50-day (7,595.72) with VIX under 25 proves the Watch stance too cautious — the bottom is confirming and the re-entry rung fires. Conversely, HY OAS above 4% with VIX above 35 proves Watch too complacent — that is a regime break, not a correction.

ladder.response: Escalation to the next zone down: no new entries, cancel any probe plans, re-check HY OAS against 4% and VIX against 35, and wait for the next zone print before reassessing.
ladder.trigger: SMH closes below $440.06 (Friday close) or NVDA below $150.49, or SPX drawdown reaches -10% from its 120-day high (~7,060)

ladder.response: Trap case confirmed: treat the bounce as a bull trap, do not chase, and cut any probe entries taken on the first bounce.
ladder.trigger: Bounce into the failure zone: SMH rallies into $580–600 or SPX into $7,750–7,820 and closes back below the zone within two sessions

ladder.response: Regime break, not a correction: stand-down in force, ladder void, no tranche deployment until a confirmed bottom forms.
ladder.trigger: Stand-down: HY OAS closes above 4%, or VIX closes above 35, or SPX closes a second week below 7,000

ladder.response: Probe per Tranche A rules on the reclaiming name only; full Add only on a confirmed bottom (failed first bounce plus a second low holding, or a held close above SPX ~7,750–7,820 / SMH ~$580–600).
ladder.trigger: Re-entry: SMH or NVDA reclaims Zone 2 on a close (SMH $470–505, NVDA $175–185) AND the mechanical tally reaches 3 of 4

reaction.trapRisk: Friday's bounce (+1.6% SPX, +4.17% SMH) printed on 0.52x average SPX volume and 0.56x SMH volume, with both names still below Zone 2 and below both moving averages and the tally at 2 of 4 — a textbook first-bounce setup. No chasing the first bounce: entries wait for the Zone 2 reclaim or for the failure-zone retest verdict (SMH $580–600 / SPX $7,750–7,820). A rejection at the failure zone confirms the trap; a hold above it confirms the turn.

strategyPosture: Watch. Friday's bounce came on half-average holiday volume with SMH and NVDA still below their buy zones and the mechanical tally at 2 of 4 — a first bounce, not a confirmed bottom. No new entries until Zone 2 is reclaimed or the next zone down prints and holds.

themes.counterRead: The divergence is real and worth tracking, not dismissing: the index-level calm masks weakness concentrated in the handful of names that dominate the index by weight. If credit conditions flip — HY OAS toward 4% — the rotation read becomes a rollover read fast. The position is to respect the rotation while it holds and watch the credit line that would void it.
themes.dataAnchor: The Mag7 average sits 19.14% below its 52-week highs against SPY only 6.8% off its high — a 12.34-point divergence gap, with AAPL just 0.6% off its high while NVDA is 38.2% off. The SPX drawdown from its 120-day high is only 6.97% (close 7,297.49 vs high 7,844.52), and bank lending standards are LOOSE at 1.7% on SLOOS, far below the ~40% stress threshold. Credit agrees: HY OAS is 3.77 and calm, not cracking.
themes.label: Rotation, not rollover — Mag7 weakness inside an intact index
themes.narrative: The tape reads as an AI-bubble unwind: the Mag7 complex is deep off its highs and the AI names dominate the laggard board, which the news frame treats as a broad market break.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS closing above 4% or the Mag7-SPX divergence gap widening past 15 points while SLOOS rises.

themes.counterRead: A sentiment-driven derating of compounding businesses is the setup the opportunity board is built for — but the derating has not stopped yet: NVDA and SMH both sit BELOW Zone 2 (NVDA $150.49 vs Zone 2 $175–185; SMH $440.06 vs Zone 2 $470–505), so the market has not yet found the floor the fundamentals imply. The gap is an opportunity only once price stops falling through the zones; until then it is a watchlist, not an entry.
themes.dataAnchor: The fundamentals run the other way. NVDA revenue is growing 61.4% YoY while the stock sits 38.2% below its high; AVGO revenue is up 55% YoY with 67.8% gross margin and $26,914M of free cash flow while 36.9% off its high; LRCX revenue is up 131.3% YoY, 56.1% off its high; ONTO revenue is up 41.5% with a 29.8% FCF margin, 53.8% off its high; DDOG revenue is up 27.7% with 80% gross margin, 44.9% off its high. PLTR, the top conviction promotion (score 81), has revenue growing 91.7% YoY with $122.25M of insider buying at the trough.
themes.label: AI infrastructure: revenue compounding while price collapses
themes.narrative: The market narrative is that AI demand has stalled — the AI gloom in the headlines — and the price action agrees: SMH is down 34.5% from its high and NVDA 38.2%, with 36 dislocations in the screen, most tagged SENTIMENT_DRIVEN.
themes.watchFor: NVDA or SMH reclaiming Zone 2 on a close (NVDA $175, SMH $470) with the mechanical tally reaching 3 of 4.

themes.counterRead: A bounce on half volume with both AI leaders still below their buy zones and both moving averages is the classic first-bounce pattern: it resolves either into a retest that holds or a failure into the next leg down. Chasing it means buying the narrative before the data confirms. The failure zone is defined — SMH $580–600, SPX $7,750–7,820 — and a bounce that reaches it and fails is the trap case.
themes.dataAnchor: The bounce printed on holiday-thin volume: SPX volume was 2.94B shares against a 20-day average of 5.64B (0.52x), and SMH volume was 7.7M against 13.8M (0.56x). SMH remains 18.31% below its 50-day and 16.3% below its 200-day; NVDA is 25.6% below its 50-day and 25.75% below its 200-day; SPX itself is still 3.93% below its 50-day and 0.77% below its 200-day. The mechanical capitulation tally is only 2 of 4 — VIX rollover and credit calm confirmed, but zone occupancy and volume climax both unconfirmed.
themes.label: Friday's bounce is a first bounce on thin volume, not a bottom
themes.narrative: Headlines call it a rally off the lows and a rare buy signal: SPX +1.6% on the day, QQQ +2.63%, SMH +4.17%, TQQQ +7.71%, with the VIX down 11.16% on the day and 33.66% over five days.
themes.watchFor: SMH volume climax with intraday reversal (volume above its 20-day average with a close in the top of the range) or a second consecutive up-day on expanding volume.

themes.counterRead: Credit and rates agree there is no funding stress today, which is why the correction reads as a growth/AI repricing rather than a credit event. The risk is a hawkish surprise on Dec 9 turning a contained repricing into a credit event — that is a binary event risk, not a trend in the data. CPI follows on Dec 10, so the two prints land back-to-back.
themes.dataAnchor: Nothing in the rates or credit data currently prices stress: the fed funds rate is 3.88, the 10-year is 4.85, the 2s10s curve is positive at +0.24, the real 10-year is 2.70, 10-year breakeven inflation is 2.15, and HY OAS is 3.77 with credit calm and not cracking. The VIX has rolled over from its 28.29 five-day high to 23.81.
themes.label: Credit calm, rates contained — the Dec 9 FOMC is the swing factor
themes.narrative: The market is bracing for a potential Fed hike at the Dec 8–9 FOMC — the highest-signal active event — with Bill Ackman saying the Fed is about to make another mistake, and the PCE print (Oct 2026) still active in the news flow.
themes.watchFor: Dec 9 FOMC decision and Dec 10 CPI print; any HY OAS move above 4% in the same window.

themes.counterRead: The narrative and the data agree here: this is a leverage unwind, not a buying opportunity yet. A 59% one-month drawdown in CONL is a position that needs a thesis re-check, not a dip buy, and the Friday bounce in these names is the same thin-volume first bounce as the rest of the tape. Size any re-entry off a confirmed bottom in the underlying (BTC/ETH stabilizing), not off a single up-day.
themes.dataAnchor: Over one month: CONL -59.08%, BMNR -37.05%, COIN -33.69%, IBIT -26.64%, ETH -26.48%, BTC -21.91%, DOGE -21.12%. All three are holdings (CONL, BMNR, DOGE), and all three still bounced with the tape on Friday (CONL +7.41%, BMNR +3.27%) without changing the one-month picture. The unwind is orderly in the sense that it is concentrated in the speculative corner — SPX is only 6.97% off its high — not a broad liquidation.
themes.label: Speculative leverage unwind: crypto complex leads the drawdown
themes.narrative: The crypto and leveraged complex is unwinding hard — the steepest one-month losses on the board are all in this corner, and the tape treats it as contagion risk for the rest of the book.
themes.watchFor: BTC and ETH stabilizing with two consecutive weekly closes above their November lows, or CONL/BMNR making a higher low on rising volume.

whereWaveBuilds: The next move builds in the AI complex: NVDA at $150.49 (-38.2% from its high, revenue +61.4% YoY) and SMH at $440.06 (-34.5%) both sit below Zone 2, so either a reclaim of Zone 2 (SMH $470–505, NVDA $175–185) or a break of Friday's lows decides whether this is a bottom forming or the correction extending. The Dec 9 FOMC decision is the macro trigger that could force either leg.
